company: walkr - turn your Google Meet walk-friendly
text:
Urban Walker
Walkr â London (or another city with strong walkability) Full-time / Part-time considered Â· On-site (outdoors)




About Walkr
Walkr helps people turn everyday calls and meetings into walks. We started as a small Chrome extension that flags walk-friendly meetings in Google Calendar, and we're building toward a bigger mission: make walking the default way people connect, think and work.
We believe most of what happens in a meeting room could happen just as well, if not better, on a pavement. We're now looking for someone to prove it, on the ground, every day.






The role
We're hiring a full-time Urban Walker: someone whose job is to walk. You'll take Walkr's calls, meetings and thinking sessions outdoors, on foot, in a city with enough walkable area to actually make that work. You'll be our internal proof of concept and our most honest source of product feedback.
Practically, this means:
Taking scheduled calls and 1:1s while walking, using Walkr to flag and organise themLogging what works and what doesn't: audio quality, routes, weather, pacing, how conversations change when nobody's looking at a screenFeeding that back into the product directly, you'll be in the room (or rather, on the street) with the team building the features you useScouting and mapping walkable routes near our hubs that others on the team can reuseOccasionally representing Walkr in walking meetings with partners, press or early users



What we're looking for
You live in, or are willing to be based in, a city with genuinely walkable areas (parks, canals, low-traffic streets, decent pavements)You're comfortable holding a normal, focused conversation while moving, this is a real skill, not everyone has itYou're organised enough to manage a calendar full of outdoor commitments and reroute around weather, meetings and lifeYou're naturally curious about behaviour change, habits and how environment shapes how we thinkBonus: you already walk a lot and have opinions about it



Why this role exists
Most companies talk about wellbeing and then put everyone back in a chair in a room with no windows. We'd rather have one person whose entire job disproves the excuse that walking meetings "don't really work in practice." If it's your job, it has to work.


What you'll get
A role that pays you to do the thing our product is trying to get everyone else to doDirect input into what we build nextFlexible hours built around daylight and your city's best routesThe rare chance to put "Professional Walker" on your CV and mean it

About This Role

Enjoy a variety of field work and office-based workOngoing, Full Time Opportunity in BendigoSalary Range $72,189 - $79,753 plus superannuation 

Do you have great communication skills and want to be a role model to people hoping for a second chance? If you want to make time to help people get their lives back on track, read on.

Who are we?

Community Work and Partnerships We are responsible for the development of mutually beneficial partnerships with government agencies and non-government organisations so that individuals can undertake unpaid work as part of their community-based sentence imposed by the Courts of Victoria. Community work serves as a valuable way for individuals to pay back the community while also reconnecting and reintegrating into the community. We ensure individuals make genuine efforts to undergo rehabilitation, and we keep low risk individuals out of prison and help them contribute to the community.

What does a Field Officer do?

Your primary responsibility as a Field Officer will be to supervise a team of clients at community work sites and other community work programs. A field officer carries out many duties and functions, mainly the supervision of individuals completing community work tasks. Other responsibilities include performing site inspections, assess hazards, providing informed workplace health and safety advice, guidance and instruction; maintaining tools and equipment resister and ensuring repairs are undertaken.

A day in the life of a Field Officer. . .

Your shift starts at a Justice Service Centre location where you collect a bus/ trailer with equipment. You then drive to a site to collect a group of clients, where you will induct, instruct and transport them to a partner not-for-profit organisation in the community. Tasks for the day may involve graffiti removal, painting, litter collection, mowing and weeding. Your responsibility is to instruct the individuals to safely perform each task and monitor the work performed for the partner site before returning them to the drop off point and returning to your depot.

We are looking for individuals with various backgrounds and experience. Some desirable skills include:

You'll need to be able to communicate and demonstrate a range of tasks and ensure a safe environment for work teams.Have a strong understanding of Occupational Health and Safety practices and their practical application.Quickly build rapport in order to understand the motivations of others, identify issues and suggest courses of action appropriate to their needs.Have demonstrated ability to manage conflict and strong problem-solving skills.Model appropriate behaviours and attitudes to assist individuals to develop new skills and work practices.Carpentry or handyman skillsGardening landscaping or painting skills

Field Officers carry out a mixture of field work and office-based work, so it's important that you are able to demonstrate computer skills and written communication skills.

Transporting individuals is also a key part of the role and Field Officers will be required to drive a 12-seater bus with trailer. A full and current drivers' licence is essential for this position.

Community Work operates seven days per week and this role will be required to work on weekends. Weekend availability is required.

For More Information About The Role Please Contact

Sarah Thompson â Manager, Community Work & Partnerships on 0407 427 396 or Sarah.Thompson@justice.vic.gov.au

How To Apply

Please click the Apply button at the bottom of this advertisement. Applications should include a resume uploaded in .doc, .docx, .pdf, .txt or .rtf formats.

The Assessment Process Will Entail The Following

Several questions in the application form upon submitting your resumeA phone screenAn interviewReference checksSecurity checksHealth assessment â medical history and physical fitness components

The successful candidate will be required to undergo pre-employment checks which may include reference checks, nationally coordinated criminal history checks (NCCHC), and misconduct screening. Dependant on the role, other checks may include VicRoads checks, drivers licence checks, medical checks, Working with Children Checks, and Declaration of Private Interests (for executive and responsible officer roles). 

If you require adjustments to the recruitment and selection process, or require an alternative format to any of the application material, please don't hesitate to get in touch with the contact person listed on this ad. 

Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people are strongly encouraged to apply.

Child Safe Statement Of Commitment

The Department of Justice and Community Safety is committed to the safety and wellbeing of children and young people. We seek to prevent harm of any kind impacting children and young people and have zero tolerance for racism, child abuse and inequality. Children and young people's rights, relationships, identity, and culture must be recognised and respected, their voices heard, and their concerns acted upon. We aim to foster a culturally safe, child safe and child friendly environment for all children and young people we have contact with, deliver services to, or are impacted by our work.

Description Trant Te-Tech design, custom build and install a wide range of high quality control panels, motor control centres (MCCs) and automation systems, offering conventional, intelligent and withdrawable systems with outstanding reliability and functionality.
We are currently looking for a proven Wireperson to join our workshop based near Totton, Southampton. 
 
The Role The Wire Person is responsible for the accurate assembly and wiring of control panels, MCCs, and automation systems in accordance with electrical drawings, specifications, and applicable standards. The role plays a key part in ensuring assemblies meet quality, safety, and compliance requirements prior to inspection and testing.What Youll Be DoingTechnical Responsibilities - Panel & MCC Wiring Carry out wiring of control panels, MCCs, and automation systems to approved schematics and wiring diagrams. Install and terminate power, control, and instrumentation cabling. Assemble and wire MCCs and control panels. Ensure correct segregation, routing and termination in line with design and compliance requirements.  Technical Support & Collaboration Accurately interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, BOMs, and general arrangement drawings. Mark up drawings where required to reflect as-built changes. Follow work instructions and build documentation. Work collaboratively with fellow wire-people, testers, and supervisors to meet production targets. Support improvements in wiring practices, layout, and efficiency.  Provide feedback to supervisors on build issues or potential improvements. SHE&Q and Compliance Carry out self-checks and peer checks prior to formal testing. Identify and report defects, non-conformances or drawing discrepancies. Work safely in accordance with company H&S procedures and UK legislation. Maintain a clean, tidy and organised working area. Use tools, equipment, and PPE correctly at all times.  Key Interfaces:
Internal Interfaces Workshop Supervisor. Production Manager. Test Engineer. Design & Engineering Teams. Automation Team. Stores / Logistic. Quality Team. External Interfaces Clients / Inspectors (as required) Suppliers (limited)  Core Values

Uphold and promote the Companys Core Values  Care, Trust, Respect and Sustainability.

 What Were Looking ForEssential NVQ Level 3 (or equivalent) in Electrical Installation, Panel Wiring, or Electrical Engineering. Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and GA drawings. Working knowledge of electrical safety practices and workshop H&S requirements. Familiarity with quality-controlled manufacturing processes. Proven experience wiring control panels, MCCs, or similar electrical assemblies. Experience terminating power, control, and instrumentation wiring. Experience working from schematics, wiring schedules, and BOMs. Experience completing work to high quality and safety standards in a workshop environment. Applicants must be legally authorised to work in the UK, as we are unable to sponsor work visas for this role. Desirable 18th Edition (BS 7671) qualification. Awareness or training relating to BS EN 61439-2:2021. Manufacturer or industry training on MCCs, switchgear andautomation systems. First Aid or IOSH Working Safely certification. Experience wiring MCCs and control panels. Experience with PLC I/O wiring, automation panels, and instrumentation. Experience supporting test and inspection activities, including rectification of faults. Experience working on custom-built, client-specific panel builds. Why Join Trant ?At Trant Engineering, we deliver complex, high-value engineering and construction projects across the UK. From process and water treatment to energy infrastructure upgrades, we play a key role in delivering and protecting critical national infrastructure  shaping the systems that communities and industries rely on every day.

Our teams design and deliver full EPC solutions, combining technical excellence with practical, hands-on delivery. We offer end-to-end capabilities  from concept and design through to manufacturing, construction and commissioning utilising a continually evolving in-house expertise. This means youll work on projects that are varied, challenging and genuinely impactful.

Our multi-disciplinary teams bring together specialists in civil, mechanical, electrical, process, instrumentation, and control & automation engineering, alongside our in-house manufacturing of control panels, MCCs, PLCs and SCADA systems. With over 1,000 people and a strong, growing pipeline of work, its an exciting time to join Trant. We are committed to helping our people succeed through our Career Development Association, providing structured support, mentoring and clear pathways to help you reach your full potential.

 Whether youre starting out or looking to take your next career step, Trant offers the chance to develop, progress and make a real difference.

 Our company benefits package includes: Competitive rates. 28 days holiday (including bank holidays). Options to buy additional holiday via salary sacrifice. Company pension scheme. Employee assistance program. Discretionary annual bonus. Join us and be part of something bigger.

SALARY: CI$50,000 - CI$70,000 pa


WORKING HOURS: 40 HOURS PER WEEK


TERM OF EMPLOYMENT: Full-Time


We are seeking a Building Maintenance Technician to join our team. The successful candidate will be responsible for the inspection, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of building infrastructure and systems to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operation of facilities.


DO YOU HAVE:


A high school diploma (or equivalent) and a valid trade license
A minimum of 5 yearsâ experience in building maintenance within Class A Commercial properties
Strong HVAC experience in chilled water and DX systems
Training and certification in electrical, plumbing, HVAC systems maintenance, Pool Operator and Man Lift operation
A valid Cayman Islands driverâs license
The ability to operate hand and power tools required, in a safe and efficient manner
Strong knowledge of building, electrical, plumbing and MEP systems, including related equipment, tools, hazards and safety precautions
Strong communication, problem-solving, and troubleshooting skills
The ability to perform physically demanding manual work for extended periods in varying and sometimes adverse conditions is required, including working in inclement weather and with regular exposure to dust and noise, as well as heavy lifting, prolonged standing, and climbing
The willingness to travel between sites, work at heights, and work outside regular business hours as required
The ability to read and interpret schematic drawings and blueprints (preferred)
A commitment to safety, continuous improvement, and professional development


WE WANT YOU TO:


Inspect, maintain, troubleshoot, and repair mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire life safety, and other building systems
Diagnose faults using schematic drawings, manuals, and blueprints, and complete corrective maintenance efficiently
Assess faulty equipment, determine repair or replacement needs, review manufacturer specifications and technical documentation, and source the required parts or materials
Adhere to the DE Engineering Health and Safety Manual and maintain accurate maintenance records

Inspect and maintain building exteriors, residential units, appliances, fixtures, pools, and site features

English at Pembroke is taught by a large, dynamic team across Years 7 to 12, spanning both SACE and the International Baccalaureate. Our teachers enjoy considerable freedom in text selection, within a framework of high academic expectations, and our faculty culture is one of collegiality, intellectual curiosity and serious engagement with pedagogy. Our staff contribute to curriculum design, and are supported to grow as practitioners at every career stage.


About the Role
Successful applicants will teach across the secondary years, with allocations shaped by experience and strengths. Depending on the appointment, this may include Middle School classes, senior SACE English subjects, or IB Diploma Language A courses.

Delivering engaging, rigorous and innovative English lessons that foster a love of learningSupporting students to develop strong literacy, analytical and communication skillsProviding purposeful assessment and feedback that supports every students' growthContributing to a positive and collaborative culture across the Middle and Senior SchoolsActively participating in the life of the School through co-curricular and pastoral care contributions.

Pembroke School is a co-educational, non-denominational, day and boarding School from Early Learning Centre to Year 12. Renowned for academic excellence and a broad, inclusive program, Pembroke offers the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE) and is also an International Baccalaureate World School, offering the IB Diploma Programme (IBDP) and Primary Years Programme (PYP).


Pembroke is a vibrant and exciting School catering for a diverse community of students. The School employs over 300 permanent and fixed-term staff, plus more than 150 casual employees.


Pembroke seeks to engage outstanding, diverse and well-qualified staff to work in our welcoming and open School. Applications for this position close on Sunday, 6 September 2026, at 11:59 pm.

Blackbird Interactive is looking for an experienced Senior Level Designer to help build and deliver high-quality gameplay spaces for an action RPG focused on fast-paced combat, character progression, exploration, and replayability. This role focuses on designing levels, encounters, and environments that create satisfying combat opportunities, reward exploration, and support a wide variety of player builds and abilities.

You'll work closely with systems design, combat design, art, narrative, audio, and engineering to create spaces that complement the game's core combat systems while providing strong pacing, readability, and a sense of discovery. The role involves collaborating with leadership to align content with the overall creative vision while owning levels end-to-end, from initial layout and blockout through implementation, iteration, and polish. As a senior designer, you'll be expected to independently solve complex level design problems, provide strong design judgment, and help establish a high quality bar for playable content across the game.


\n


Responsibilities


Collaborate with combat, systems, narrative, art, engineering, audio, and production to create levels that support the established creative vision and core gameplay pillars



Own levels end-to-end, including layouts, blockouts, combat spaces, encounters, traversal, exploration, pacing, and player flow



Design engaging combat spaces that support varied enemies, character builds, abilities, positioning, and different approaches to combat



Create rewarding exploration through optional paths, secrets, environmental storytelling, and meaningful rewards while maintaining clear navigation and progression



Script and implement gameplay events, encounters, objectives, triggers, and environmental interactions directly in engine



Test, debug, and iterate on levels using playtest feedback to improve combat flow, difficulty, pacing, readability, and replayability





Requirements


A minimum of 8 years of game development experience, with significant experience designing and implementing levels for action, RPG, or combat focused games



Experience shipping multiple titles, including at least one in a senior or equivalent level design role



Proven ability to independently own complex levels from initial concept and blockout through implementation, iteration, and final polish



Strong understanding of action RPG level design, including combat spaces, encounter pacing, exploration, progression, player guidance, and replayability



Strong hands-on experience with level editing, gameplay scripting, and in-engine implementation, with the ability to prototype, debug, and iterate quickly



Strong design judgment, communication, and collaboration skills, with the ability to balance gameplay quality, creative goals, technical constraints, and production realities





Pluses


Passion for action RPGs centered on combat, character builds, loot, progression, and exploration



Experience designing levels for an isometric or elevated gameplay camera, with an understanding of its impact on combat readability, navigation, and composition



Experience creating replayable content that supports different character builds, abilities, difficulty levels, or repeated playthroughs



Appreciation for systemic combat and how level geometry, enemy composition, hazards, and interactive elements combine to create varied encounters



Experience designing dungeons, interconnected environments, procedural or modular level content, or other repeatable gameplay spaces



Strong instincts for environmental storytelling, gameplay readability, polish, and identifying opportunities to improve the player experience through iteration
